title: The Pigeon Who Became A War Hero
description:
Cher Ami was a male homing pigeon known for his service in World War I, especially the Meuse-Argonne offensive in October 1918. He was one of 600 English-bred birds donated to the U.S. Army Signal Corps' Pigeon Service in May 1918. According to popular legend, he delivered a message alerting American forces to the location of the Lost Battalion despite being shot in the breast, losing his right leg and being blinded in one eye. He flew about 25 miles back to his loft in 25 minutes, was treated by army medics and shipped to the United States. He received France's Croix de Guerre medal for delivering 12 important messages at Verdun, but contrary to news reports he did not receive a Distinguished Service Cross.

Source: Wikipedia, 'Cher Ami'. Some details of the legend are disputed.
